source_text: Dicimus has, quae nunc aguntur in orbe terrarum, a Deo nuptias institutas nec reos esse coniuges, sed fornicatores et adulteros condemnandos.
pass_a_gloss: We say that these marriages which are now carried on in the circle of the lands were instituted by God, and that spouses are not guilty, but fornicators and adulterers are to be condemned.

lemmas.lexica: LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: We say that the marriages now taking place throughout the world were instituted by God. Married people are not guilty; it is those who commit sexual immorality and adultery who should be condemned.

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (Letter to Rome, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 1); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
